- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive (sentiment > 0.5) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or neutral (sentiment < 0.5) — model is overly conservative, missing upward momentum.
- Forecast tends to lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days, especially in the early part of the 30-day horizon — adjust for delayed reaction to sentiment shifts.
- Mean reversion bias: model overreacts to short-term sentiment swings, leading to overcorrection in direction — reduce volatility in forecast if sentiment is stable.
- When sentiment is consistently positive over 3+ days, model should not over-forecast beyond 10–15% above recent high — cap upward bias to avoid overextension.
- If sentiment is negative and price is trending up, model often underestimates the reversal — adjust downward by 2–5% of recent high if sentiment turns negative.
- Forecast horizon 30d: model tends to overestimate later days (days 20–30) when sentiment is positive — reduce forecast slope in later days if sentiment is trending flat or slightly positive.
